title: Chapter 207: Black or White?
html:
“Did you find the white figure?” As the woman left the bedroom, her expression transformed. Her lashes trembled against her pallid face, making her look every inch a damsel in distress.

“No.” Gu Feiyu glanced at her uncovered face, grew visibly awkward, and looked away.

“Sit down. I suspect there’s more behind the white figure’s appearance.” She invited Gu Feiyu onto the sofa, then kicked off her heels and walked barefoot into the kitchen.

Gu Feiyu gripped his baton with both hands. Agitation showed in his face, and his legs trembled. The woman retrieved two already-open bottles from the refrigerator and set them on the coffee table. “Thank you for helping me tonight.”

“Just doing my job.” Gu Feiyu was embarrassed.

“No, I truly owe you thanks. Without you, I wouldn’t have known what to do. Since my older sister disappeared, I’ve been alone in Jiujiang. I have little money. Once this apartment sells, I’ll leave for good.” She sat opposite him, still seemingly frightened, curled her legs along the sofa’s edge, and gently massaged them.

“Leaving may be for the best.” Gu Feiyu nodded, pity coloring his gaze. “But don’t lose hope. Your sister is only missing. She may return someday.”

“It isn’t that simple. My sister and I were extremely close. We grew up together. She shared everything with me, every secret, and then one day she simply vanished. I fear she’s already…” Her voice broke. She seemed to force the confession out, baring herself to a stranger.

Her slight frame and slender limbs made her appear terribly fragile. When she began to cry, Gu Feiyu became flustered. Unsure what else to do, he set down his baton and offered her the tissue box. She accepted one and dabbed carefully around her eyes to preserve her makeup. “When I came home and saw the white figure, I was terrified. Do you think it took my sister?”

Despair saturated her voice. “Now that I’ve seen it, will it take me next?”

“It won’t.” Apparently lost in grief, she did not notice how far her skirt had fallen open. Gu Feiyu saw and immediately averted his gaze.

“I hope you’re right.” She lifted her drink and tapped it lightly against Gu Feiyu’s bottle. “I’m sorry to burden you with this.”

She drank. Coming back to himself, Gu Feiyu took a polite sip as well.

“You shouldn’t be so pessimistic. Several people have asked about your sister these past few days, so I’m sure she’s alive. Perhaps something prevents her from contacting you.”

The chilled drink tasted refreshing, and Gu Feiyu took another swallow without thinking. “Your sister probably had reasons for leaving. I don’t believe in ghosts. Maybe she made a mistake and went into hiding. I feel sorry for her, really. If she can’t even see the person who loves her most, what kind of life is that?”

“You don’t understand her. None of you ever tried.” Sadness filled her face, though something shifted in her voice. “She was the best older sister anyone could ask for. She even shared her most precious possession with me.”

A sudden exhaustion overcame Gu Feiyu. Hugging his baton, he slumped against the sofa. “You two must have been very close.”

The woman seemed to sink into memory, though her gaze never left his half-empty bottle. “When I was young, other children bullied me, and my sister always defended me. As we grew older, our personalities diverged. I was selfish and temperamental, but no matter what I did, she forgave me. She was perfect—beautiful, graceful, with a radiant smile.

“I didn’t appreciate her then. The more tolerant she was, the more I resented her. I rejected everything she loved. She liked white, so I chose black. I had to be her opposite. It continued for months, until the incident.”

She studied the guard in silence before continuing. “I hate to admit it, but we fell in love with the same person.

“A handsome boy in our neighborhood fell in love with my sister. He listened to music, composed songs, and sang beautifully. Whenever they went out together, it felt as though a thousand knives carved into my heart. I could not allow the person I loved to belong to someone else.

“My sister and I looked alike, so I copied her makeup and wore her clothes. At first, I fooled him, but eventually he discovered the truth. I wasn’t my sister; our personalities were entirely different. I cried and begged him to stay, but he loved only her.”

Veins stood out grotesquely along her arms, but Gu Feiyu no longer seemed to notice. His eyelids kept drooping, as though the night patrol had exhausted him.

“For his sake, I swallowed my pride and begged my sister, but the sister who claimed to love me said nothing. We did not speak for a week. In the end, she compromised. She would invite the boy over and make him choose.

“Her invitation delighted him. He bought a new shirt and fresh flowers, then spent the entire night recording her favorite song. When he arrived, he confessed at once. She did not answer. Instead, she called me out and told him to choose.

“My sister was wearing her favorite white dress, so I wore black. She asked the boy, ‘Honey, white or black, which color do you prefer?’

“I had never prayed so desperately, yet within seconds, every hope shattered. He chose my sister without hesitation.”

Her nails dug into her palms. Even after so many years, the betrayal remained raw. Her breathing turned ragged and took a long time to settle. “It felt as though my heart had been torn open. No words can describe that pain. I wanted to flee somewhere no one could find me.

“My sister saw my pain. She seemed to have expected the outcome. At the lowest moment of my life, she once again stepped forward to help me. She gave the boy a bottle of water, removed her white dress, and went to the kitchen for a cleaver.

“She told me that other than white and black, there was another choice that was fairest to all.”

The woman fell silent and drew a cleaver from beneath the sofa. With the tissue Gu Feiyu had given her, she wiped the makeup from her face. Reliving that long-ago night, she raised the blade and approached his motionless body. Her wig slipped away, and her completely hairless face bent close to his ear.

“Honey, black, white, and red, which color do you prefer?”
